<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/your-first-project.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78defe2aa87aa9583a3a8d5b33ad10997d577d5b` — the merge of head `55668474107ba329f67b5aa603e0734c70c44960` into base `fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78defe2aa87aa9583a3a8d5b33ad10997d577d5b && git checkout 78defe2aa87aa9583a3a8d5b33ad10997d577d5b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048 55668474107ba329f67b5aa603e0734c70c44960 && git checkout -B drift-repro fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048 && git merge --no-ff 55668474107ba329f67b5aa603e0734c70c44960

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review · 2026-11-17T13:28Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: b5554ad9cb0f14d2eb02af5e2d4bccc55559efb8

Read at this exact head: the 21 files (+754/−64), the body, card #34718, claim 6945562353, amendments 6947260430 and 6948706504, and os-dev-reports 6947204107 and 6948675399.

**Tier H.** `check-governed-merges`: GOVERNED (3 of 21 paths hit the register, `skills/objectstack-ui/**`), 818 lines. This L1 does not ready it. The seat's L2 at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER comes next, then os-zhuang.

Check-runs on this sha: 74 total, 62 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed or pending.

### Must-fix

None.

### Should-fix

- **S1: the dataset guides teach the shape this rule now warns on, and the main one never names the two keys.** `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx` (~:53-69), the "Guides → Analytics Datasets" page that `dashboards.md` points to, declares 3 dimensions and 5 measures with neither `synonyms` nor `description`. That is 8 findings for a reader who copies it, and the page never mentions either key. `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx` (~:220-233, `salesDataset`) adds 4 more. The os-dev report lists these as out-of-scope with `carrier: none`. Nothing on these pages becomes literally false, but the canonical example now draws the advisory this PR adds, and the guide stays silent on how to clear it. Close it one of two ways:
  - (a) in this PR, under a claim amendment: add `synonyms` and/or `description` to those members and one line naming `dataset-member-no-vocabulary` in analytics.mdx; or
  - (b) file a carrier (the epic seat's follow-up card for example descriptions could take it) and cite it in the body.

  Under the nit-only landing standard, this must not stay open with no carrier.

### Checklist

- **Shape:** draft, `Closes #34718`. Both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) are in the body and the changeset, and they match the claim. The new `@objectstack/lint` exports (`validateDatasetMemberVocabulary`, `DATASET_MEMBER_NO_VOCABULARY`, the finding type) follow the per-rule barrel convention (`rule-id-barrel-exports.test.ts`). The precedent is #32202 (advisory rule, `Clause-②: no`). Whether that convention keeps `no` on a governed PR is the seat's L2 face.
- **Surface:**
  - Inside claim 6945562353: lint src and tests, `dashboards.md` and its evals, the four transcript pages and the three example datasets.
  - Covered by amendments: `generate.ts` (6947260430), the metadata-protocol fixture test, and `generate-binds-from-stack.test.ts` (6948706504).
  - `packages/cli/test/generate-permission-dataset.pin.test.ts` is not named in either amendment. It is the scaffold's exact-output pin, which falls under 6947260430's "the scaffold test" intent. Note N1.
  - No unrelated files.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/skills` (`packages/skills/package.json`), all at patch. These are the three published packages whose content moved. `metadata-protocol` and `examples/**` changed tests and data only.
- **Rule:**
  - It is warning-only everywhere: `tier: 'advisory'`, `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['dataset']`, and the finding type pins `severity: 'warning'`.
  - It reads only the member's own `synonyms` and `description`, so it is safe on the unparsed `os lint` stack and on the per-write snapshot.
  - A blank-only synonyms list or a blank locale map does not count as declared, which matches the explanation text.
  - Placing it after the two dataset rules with `input: 'parsed'` follows their stated rationale.
- **Scaffold:**
  - Seeds come from declared labels, used as written. `normalizeDatasetTerm` (the schema's own fold) keeps one word on one member, and the fallback candidates mean the scaffold always parses.
  - `generate-scaffold-validates.test.ts` is unchanged and still demands zero findings.
  - The non-English measurement (发票 / 发票号) is in the report.
- **Tests:**
  - Real commands: lint passes 216 files / 9136 tests; lint and cli typecheck pass; the three generate files pass 74 tests at this head.
  - The whole CLI unit tier was not rerun at this head, because the last commit edits only that pin. CI's Test Core is green on this sha.
  - The round-0 ablation on the rule guard stands.
- **Docs made false:** the four transcript counts move 69 → 70, matching the changeset. For teaching drift, see S1. The skills text is within the token ratchet (`check-skills-token-ratchet` exit 0 in the report). The new eval (id 9, a Chinese brief) asserts a flat list and no locale-keyed map, consistent with ADR-0149 D1.
- **UI strings:** none.

### Notes

- N1: Name `generate-permission-dataset.pin.test.ts` in the next amendment or in the body's surface list. It is a pin the scaffold change moved.
- N2: The overlap with draft #34791 (the transcript count and `authoring-rules.ts`) is known. Whichever lands second re-derives the count, per 6948706504.
- N3: The system datasets in `packages/platform-objects` declare neither key on 7 members, but `os lint` over its extract config reports 0 findings of this rule (per the report). If those datasets ever reach a door that runs it, they will draw 7 warnings.
- N4: The example datasets carry `synonyms` only. Descriptions and bundle translations go to a seat-filed card, an accepted deviation (6947260430). That card has no number yet.

## L1 delta review · 2026-11-17T14:43Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: 80edbdae04cb635783baaa91a9f88bb601377a48

This is a delta from my ACCEPT 6949452870 at `b5554ad9`, and it supersedes that verdict. The delta is one commit, docs only: `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx` and `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`, +46/−12. Read with seat amendment 6949469635 (option a), report 6950232135 and the flake note 6950658738.

**Still Tier H** (governed by `skills/objectstack-ui/**`; the file list beyond these two docs is unchanged). This L1 does not ready it. The seat's L2 at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER comes next, then os-zhuang.

Check-runs on this sha: all completed, 0 failed. The one Test Core (6/10) lint-timeout re-run is green; see the note.

### Must-fix

None.

### Should-fix

None. **S1 is fixed.**
- `analytics.mdx`:
  - All 8 example members now carry vocabulary: synonyms on all 8, and a description on 4 of the 5 measures.
  - A new bullet teaches the flat, untranslated synonyms list, the one-word-one-member rule and the `description` as a business definition.
  - The bullet names `dataset-member-no-vocabulary` at validation and publish.
- `dashboards.mdx`: all 4 `salesDataset` members now carry synonyms, and `revenue` also has a description.

### Delta checklist

- **Correctness of the new examples:**
  - Within each dataset, no synonym folds onto another member's name, label or synonym, under the `normalizeDatasetTerm` fold (case, width, spacing, `_`/`-`). In analytics: `pipeline stage`/`phase`, `territory`/`area`, `close month`/`closing date`, `deals`/`opportunities`/`number of deals`, `sales`/`pipeline value`, `won revenue`/`bookings`, `close rate`/`conversion rate`, `sales cycle`/`time to close`. In dashboards: `territory`/`area`, `closing month`/`month closed`, `sales`/`pipeline value`, `deals`/`number of deals`.
  - The dataset name `sales` in dashboards.mdx is not a member, so the `revenue` synonym `sales` is legal.
  - The descriptions are plain business definitions, not prompts.
  - Each member declares at least one key, so neither example draws the advisory.
- **Surface:** both pages are added by amendment 6949469635. No other file moved.
- **Changeset:** unchanged. Docs need none.
- **Docs made false:** none. The new bullet matches the rule's explanation text and the changeset.

### Notes

The earlier N1–N4 stand unchanged: the `generate-permission-dataset.pin.test.ts` surface line, the #34791 count overlap, the `platform-objects` system datasets, and the number for the example-descriptions card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80edbdae04cb635783baaa91a9f88bb601377a48`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ui/evals/README.md, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/analytics-inline-vs-dataset.json, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md + packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-member-vocabulary.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts
Security-touching: no

Read for this record: card #34718 (body and all nine comments: triage 6942773436 and 6944629941, claim 6945562353, reports 6947204107, 6948675399 and 6950232135, amendments 6947260430, 6948706504 and 6949469635), PR #34822 (body, 23 files, net diff against `main` from merge-base `3bbda33b78`, PR comments including L1 6949452870 and L1 delta 6951339675), and the check-runs on this head: every run completed, none failed (success or skipped throughout). Cited code was read on `main`: `packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/dataset.json`, `docs/adr/0149-*`, `packages/lint/src/rule-id-barrel-exports.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/collection-entries.ts`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged. Right.** No schema file moves. The new rule is `tier: 'advisory'` and its finding type pins `severity: 'warning'`, so nothing that parsed, built or published before is refused now. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, value or type is added, narrowed or changed in meaning.
- **`@objectstack/lint` public surface: widened by three names on the `.` entry. Declared wrong** (see ②). `packages/lint/src/index.ts` adds `validateDatasetMemberVocabulary`, `DATASET_MEMBER_NO_VOCABULARY` and the `DatasetMemberVocabularyFinding` type.
- **`AUTHORING_RULES` gains one entry and `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` one key. Right, and additive.** The rule count the CLI prints goes 69 to 70; the four transcript pages move with it and `check:docs-transcript-drift` is green in CI on this head.
- **Publish door for a `dataset` write: the save response can now carry this advisory. Right.** `runtimeTypes: ['dataset']`, existing advisory shape, zero errors; the differential cancels a stored sibling. No new response field.
- **`os generate dataset` output changes. Right, behaviour only.** `ScaffoldObjectBinding.displayFieldLabel` is new and optional; the CLI entry exports only the command default, so the interface is not on a published surface.
- **`@objectstack/skills`: teaching text and one eval. Right at patch.**

### ② Semver level

Levels are right: `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/skills` each at `patch`, the three published packages whose shipped content moves; `metadata-protocol` and `examples/**` move tests and data only. With `Metadata-protocol: none` every entry is `patch` (ruling A, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`), and that stays true whatever the `Clause-②:` line reads. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

S1 (should-fix) — the `Clause-②: no` line is wrong; three new exports of a published package are a widening.

- The criterion is written down and it is not about intent: `Clause-②` asks whether the change widens what a published package exposes, and the public surface is what the built entry declarations reach, starting with the re-exported names (`references/execution-duties.md`, and CONTRIBUTING.md Human Minimum 5: "its accept set or public surface"). `@objectstack/lint` is published (18.5.0, `exports["."]`), and after this PR a consumer can import three names it could not import before.
- The tree itself calls them public. The barrel comment added by this PR says the rule id "is published for `--json` consumers"; the test it cites, `rule-id-barrel-exports.test.ts`, opens with "Public-surface contract (#5648)" and exists precisely because a rule id no barrel re-exports is unreachable to consumers; and the changeset body announces the three exports to readers. An export that is announced in release notes for consumers to compare against is not internal.
- "Per-rule barrel convention" explains why the exports exist, not why they would not count. The precedents (#32202, and `.changeset/34567-form-layout-inline-edit-bulk.md` in the tree today) made the same declaration; they are the same misreading, not a rule. They are not re-opened here; the seat may want one ruling so the next rule PR does not repeat it.
- What it costs if left: the release body groups this entry under 其他修复 where a non-breaking `Clause-②: yes` widening belongs under 新增能力 (`docs/releases-maintenance.md`), and a wrong `no` is an auditable false declaration (`references/landing-operations.md`). It does not change a level, a gate verdict or the review tier, which is why it is not graded higher.
- The fix, on the prose faces only. In `.changeset/34718-dataset-member-vocabulary-advisory.md` and in the PR body, replace the `Clause-②: no` line with:

  `Clause-②: yes (widening) — @objectstack/lint gains three exports on its "." entry: validateDatasetMemberVocabulary, DATASET_MEMBER_NO_VOCABULARY and the DatasetMemberVocabularyFinding type; nothing accepted before is refused`

  `Metadata-protocol: none` stays as it is, on both. All three levels stay `patch`. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker: the arm is `(widening)`. The claim comment 6945562353 also reads `Clause-②: no` and the entry gate reads the claim, so the seat corrects it by amendment in the same stroke. The changeset edit moves the head; the delta record names S1 closed on the new head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **SQL push-down: nothing to judge.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the rule is a pure read of the stack document.
- **Open question 1, the scaffold (Gap 1 = A, amendment 6947260430): the ruling holds, with one residual named.** B and C would each have cut a hole in the zero-finding scaffold contract, and A keeps `generate-scaffold-validates.test.ts` unchanged. The schema does accept a synonym equal to its own member's name or label (`checkDatasetVocabulary`: "accepted as written (redundant, harmless)"), so the scaffold parses. The residual: where the stack declares no label for the title field, the seed is the title-cased field name, and the pinned default is dimension `name` with `synonyms: ['Name']`. Under `normalizeDatasetTerm` that folds to the member's own name, so it adds no word the matcher did not already have, and it silences the advisory on a member that still "answers only to its own name and label". The measure seed (the object's plural label, pinned `Account` beside label `Records`) and a declared field label (`发票号` on `invoice_no`) are real added words. So a scaffolded dataset never draws this advisory, and the comment above the members is the only prompt to replace the seed. That is the trade the seat ruled, the scaffold's comment and the changeset both say so in words, and I accept it as an accepted deviation. Whether the rule should one day read a synonym that folds to its own name or label as no vocabulary is a design question for the epic seat; it would re-open this scaffold ruling and is not owed here.
- **Open question 2, examples carry `synonyms` without `description` (Gap 2 = A): accepted deviation, holds.** One key silences the rule by its contract, the measured i18n-coverage growth (106 to 124 on app-todo) is a real reason to keep translation work out of a data-only surface, and `examples/app-crm` still shows the complete form. Owed by the seat before landing: the follow-up card the amendment promised (descriptions plus bundle translations, to be filed by epic:#34659#1) has no number yet in any comment or in the PR body; an accepted deviation with no carrier is not closed.
- **Overlap with draft #34791: accepted as stated.** The conflict is textual, on the four transcript count lines plus `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` and `index.ts`. Whichever lands second merges `main` and re-derives the count. If that is this PR, the merge moves two files inside this record's scope, so the new head owes a delta record; this record covers `80edbdae04` only.
- **Dev deviations.** `packages/cli/test/generate-binds-from-stack.test.ts` and `generate-permission-dataset.pin.test.ts` are covered by amendments 6948706504 and 6949469635. The CLI unit tier and the four gates the dev did not rerun locally are answered by CI: Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, the Lint families and Type Check are all green on this head. The one red on this head (Test Core 6/10, a 5000 ms timeout in `validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts`) was rerun once and is green; the file is outside this diff.
- **For the lane seat, outside ④ and ungraded: the PR body's acceptance note 5 is not true of the tree.** It says `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx` no longer teaches bare members. The page has a second dataset, `projectTasksDataset` at about :701, whose 3 dimensions and 3 measures declare neither key, so a reader who copies it draws six findings. L1's docs finding (6949452870) and amendment 6949469635 named only `salesDataset` at :220-233, so the amended surface was met, but the sentence in the body overstates it. It is a docs prose face, the lane seat's to judge: fix the six members there, or correct the sentence and name a carrier.
- **Noted, no action owed here:** the seven bare members of the platform's own system datasets (`packages/platform-objects`), carrier none, outside the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

S1 above is the one graded finding on this head and it sits on the declaration, not on the design. On the `hits` files and the implementing files the design holds; what follows are nits.

**`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md`**, against the card's scope sentence and the spec on `main`. Holds.
- The card asks for: the words a person types, in the language of the request, a one-sentence business definition, one word names one member. The rewritten comment says each of the four, and names the rule id. The spec agrees: synonyms are a flat list matched after `normalizeDatasetTerm` and never translated; `description` is a business definition, never a prompt.
- The example still type-checks and parses (`check:skill-examples` green in CI) and no longer draws the warning it teaches: `signed_date` gains `synonyms: ['签约月']`, which collides with nothing in the dataset.
- What the rewrite dropped is still taught where a reader needs it. "Every language in one list" survives in the example itself (`['签约数', 'deals signed']`) and in the rule's hint and explanation; "translated like `label`" is in `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:183`, which also says synonyms have no key.
- "One-sentence" is narrower than the spec's "one or two sentences"; it is the card's wording and nothing refuses a second sentence.
- N1 (nit) — "Neither warns: `dataset-member-no-vocabulary`" reads two ways: "a member with neither draws the warning" (meant) or "neither key warns". The instruction before it ("Every member: ...") is unambiguous, so authored output does not change. The file sits at its token ceiling (6232 of 6232), which is why it is this terse. Left as an accepted deviation; a later edit of this file can spend two tokens on "With neither:".

**`skills/objectstack-ui/evals/analytics-inline-vs-dataset.json`**, against the card's done-when ("an eval case covers a Chinese brief and expects Chinese synonyms"). Holds.
